title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Nursing Education: Perceived Barriers Among South African Nurse Educators and Nursing Students
content: Background/Objectives: This study investigates the perceived barriers to integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into nursing education among nurse educators and nursing students at a public higher education institution in Gauteng, South Africa. Methods: A qualitative, exploratory, descriptive, contextual design was employed. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 12 nurse educators and 28 third-year nursing students. Data collection was conducted through semi-structured interviews with nurse educators and focus group discussions with nursing students. The data were analysed thematically, utilising Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework, with the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology(UTAUT) serving as an interpretative lens. Results: Four interrelated barriers emerged: infrastructure and resource constraints; limited AI literacy and skills; resistance and readiness challenges; and governance, ethical, and regulatory concerns. These barriers collectively influenced participants' willingness and capacity to engage with AI in nursing education. Conclusions: The effective integration of AI into nursing education necessitates coordinated institutional responses that address infrastructure, AI literacy, organisational readiness, and ethical governance. Developing contextually relevant policies, ensuring equitable access to technology, providing continuous professional development, and offering appropriate technical support may foster a more conducive environment for the responsible and sustainable integration of AI into nursing education.
